NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular
  business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a
  recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35
  (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 14, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR HUFF at 7:05 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Laura Diepenbrock and Judy Bayer from Palos Verdes Peninsula Village.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Services Supervisory Pinuelas

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING FEBRUARY 2023 AS BLACK HISTORY MONTH

MAYOR HUFF declared February 2023 as Black History Month.

B.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING FEBRUARY 2023 AS AMERICAN HEART MONTH

MAYOR HUFF declared February 2023 as American Heart Month.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 4A-G AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JANUARY 24, 2023

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF JANUARY 2023 & FEBRUARY 2023

  APPROVED WARRANTS 65879 THROUGH 65976 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $602,651.29 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 020123 THROUGH
  020323; IN THE AMOUNT OF $119,329.25 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $721,980.54 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
FEBRUARY 14, 2023
 D.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 6, 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF JANUARY 17, 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  2022-23 BIANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT, JULY 1, 2022 TO JANUARY
  31, 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS BOARD MEETING
  HIGHLIGHTS OF JANUARY 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

None.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PUBLIC HEARING - RESOLUTION NO. 2540 APPROVING THE PROPOSED USE
  OF FY 2023-24 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) open the Public Hearing; 2) receive any
  public testimony; 3) close the Public Hearing; 4) waive further reading and approve
  Resolution No. 2540 authorizing execution of a contract with the Los Angeles County
  Community Development Commission for participation in the program for funding of
  the ADA Access Ramp and Sidewalk Improvement Program as identified in the
  Program and Conditions Assessment Report dated April 2, 2014 in the amount of
  approximately $20,151.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

Public Works Director Wahba explained that he and the County of Los Angeles Public Works
Department inspect the areas to identify what needs repair based on the 2014 Program and
Condition Assessment Report, and then the County calculates what the cost will be, in
response to MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ.

Public Works Director Wahba explained that there was no plan to change the City’s use of
CDBG funds for future years, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

Discussion ensued about possible uses for the CDBG funds.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION NO. 2540 AUTHORIZING EXECUTION OF A
  CONTRACT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION FOR PARTICIPATION IN THE PROGRAM
  FOR FUNDING OF THE ADA ACCESS RAMP AND SIDEWALK

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 14, 2023
   IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM AS IDENTIFIED IN THE PROGRAM AND
  CONDITIONS ASSESSMENT REPORT DATED APRIL 2, 2014 IN THE
  AMOUNT OF APPROXIMATELY $20,151.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

Assistant City Manager Davis read the Resolution by title.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PRESENTATION OF STORMWATER DRY WELL SITING STUDY BY GEOSYNTEC
  CONSULTING INC.; AND, AMENDED PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
  (PSA) TO FURTHER RETAIN GEOSYNTEC TO ASSIST WITH PROJECT
  ENGNIEERING, PREPARATION AND AWARD OF BID, AND CONSTRUCTION
  MANAGEMENT

  Recommendation: Presentation of stormwater dry well siting study by Geosyntec
  Consulting Inc.; and, amended Professional Services Agreement (PSA) to further
  retain Geosyntec to assist with project engineering, preparation and award of bid, and
  construction management

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Consultant Curtis Fang with Geosyntec provided a PowerPoint presentation outlining the study.

Consultant Fang explained the “expenses” column in the report, and the typical 10% markup
that Geosyntec adds to expenses, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ.

Public Works Director Wahba explained that the project would be funded with federal American
Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER.

Consultant Fang explained that they would work with the City on establishing the construction
hours for the project, as well as traffic control during the week, and do not plan for any weekend
work, in response to MAYOR HUFF.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE REPORT FROM GEOSYNTEC CONSULTANTS, INC. ON
  THEIR DRY WELL SITING STUDY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE AN AMENDED PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (PSA)
  WITH GEOSYNTEC CONSULTANTS, INC. TO CARRY OUT THE PROJECT’S
  FINAL ENGINEERING SPECIFICATIONS AND PLANS, PREPARATION OF
  BID DOCUMENTS, AND CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT FOR THE
  INSTALLATION OF TWO NEW DRY WELLS, IN THE TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF$178,900 (USING MEASURE W FUNDS), ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF
  THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 14, 2023
 B.  A LOS ANGELES COUNTY GENERAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (GSA) 5-YEAR
  RENEWAL FOR SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached General Services
  Agreement (GSA) between the City of Rolling Hills Estates and the County of Los
  Angeles, which would go into effect on July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2028.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,
  TO APPROVE BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE GENERAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (GSA) BETWEEN THE
  CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES AND THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES,
  WHICH WOULD GO INTO EFFECT ON JULY 1, 2023 THROUGH JUNE 30,
  2028.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO ADJOURN TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD
  MEETING.

**ADJOURN TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD MEETING**

A.  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION FINANCIALS OVERVIEW 2019-2022

  Recommendation: That the Rolling Hills Estates Pepper Tree Foundation Executive
  Board of Directors receive and file this report.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER thanked staff for the complete report.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

B.  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION WEBSITE OUTREACH

  Recommendation: That the Rolling Hills Estates Pepper Tree Foundation Executive
  Board of Directors approve the development of a Pepper Tree Foundation website
  and authorize the Executive Director/City Manager to enter into an Agreement with
  Tripepi Smith for the development and hosting of the new website in the amount of
  $9,980 and $580 annually thereafter.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
FEBRUARY 14, 2023
 COUNCIL MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER expressed concerned about the visibility of the
Pepper Tree Foundation page within the City’s website, and wants to be sure to retain the
purpose of the Foundation.

MAYOR HUFF felt that a new website separate from the City’s website was premature.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA agreed with much of what COUNCIL MEMBER BROWN
SCHACHTER stated, and is concerned that about losing sight of the goal of the Foundation to
raise money. She stated that she would rather see some money spent to help the new Pepper
Tree Foundation Fundraising Committee raise funds for the Foundation, and possibly a
separate Link on the City’s website for the public art project.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ expressed concern about separating URLs, and stated she
would rather put money into a multi-layer outreach campaign for fundraising rather than a new
separate website for the Foundation.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN supports keeping the Pepper Tree Foundation within the
City’s website, while making it more visible than it is today. He stated that websites do raise
money, but that requires continuous campaigns.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER BROWN
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  TABLE FOR DISCUSSION AT A FUTURE MEETING.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

Assistant City Manager confirmed that in the meantime, staff will make the current Pepper
Tree Foundation webpage within the City’s website more visible.

C.  REQUEST FOR A 19TH AMENDMENT COMMEMORATION PLAQUE

  Recommendation: That the Pepper Tree Foundation Executive Board of Directors
  consider the proposal for recognition commemorating the 100th Anniversary of the
  certification of the 19th Amendment to the United States Constitution, which granted
  women the right to vote, and provide direction to staff.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  CONSENSUS OF COUNCIL TO MOVE FORWARD WITH THE REQUESTED
  RECOGNITION PLAQUE.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

D.  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION FUNDRAISING COMMITTEE APPOINTMENT

  Recommendation: That the Rolling Hills Estates Pepper Tree Foundation Executive
  Board of Directors appoint Mr. Steve Zuckerman to the Fundraising Committee.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
FEBRUARY 14, 2023
 Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  APPOINT MR. STEVEN ZUCKERMAN TO THE FUNDRAISING COMMITTEE.

The motion was approved by acclamation.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO RECONVENE THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING:

**RECONVENE TO CITY COUNCIL MEETING MEETING**

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ will be attending the California Contract Cities Associations
monthly Board meeting on Thursday in Monterey Park.

MAYOR HUFF attended the West Basin Municipal Water District’s Director Installation
Ceremony in Carson.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  COMMITTEE APPOINTMENTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council make appointments to fill the one (1) vacancy
  on the Environmental Advisory Committee and two (2) vacancies on the Traffic & Safety
  Committee from the recently interviewed candidates.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

Discussion ensued about the applicants, current vacancies, and the vacancy that exists on the
Park & Activities Commission.

COUNCIL MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER noted that Susan Robinson had elected to
remain on the Equestrian Committee.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPOINT SIMONE SCHMIDT TO THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY
  COMMITTEE; APPOINT RENA NASH AND GARY MANCUSO TO THE
  TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:49 PM MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of Jackie Crowley.
The meeting was adjourned to Tuesday, February 28, 2023, at 7:00 PM for the purpose of
a Regular Meeting.
  [signatures on next page]

FEBRUARY 14, 2023
 Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Britt Huff
City Clerk  Mayor
